sections.title: Fill in the blanks and write the correct answers.

questions.q: ________ icing is made from icing sugar and warm water.
Butter ________ is a mix of butter and icing sugar.
On wedding cakes, we usually apply ________ icing.
Piping bags are made by using ________ paper.
________ is a clay like paste made out of ground almonds.
________ icing is used for both icing cakes and making cake decorations.
Buttercream can be stored at ________ temperature.
A ________ bag requires a nozzle.
In cream icing the amount of sugar should be ________ per cent of the amount of cream.
A cake decorated with cream icing can be stored in a refrigerator for a maximum of ________ days.

sections.title: State whether the following statements are True or False.

questions.q: Marzipan is almond paste.
A piping bag may be prepared with grease proof paper.
A cake turntable helps in icing a cake.
Butter icing can be stored at room temperature for a fortnight.
questions.answer: True. The room should be well ventilated.

questions.q: Glace icing can be prepared and kept for later use.
questions.answer: False. It sets very quickly and should be used immediately.

questions.q: 'Marzipan' is chocolate based.
questions.answer: False. It is made from almonds and sugar.

questions.q: Marzipan is heated and poured over cakes.
questions.answer: False. It is rolled out and used to cover cakes.

questions.q: A cake comb is a decorative tool.
A 'Cake base' makes it easy to handle the cake during and after decoration.
Buttercream is a mix of egg yolk, butter and flour.
questions.answer: False. It is a mix of butter (fat) and icing sugar.

questions.q: Royal icing is beaten with an egg beater to incorporate air.
questions.answer: False. It is beaten with a fork.

sections.title: Answer the following questions (five points each).

questions.q: Discuss the tools required for icing a cake.
questions.answer: (i) Grease proof paper and piping bags with nozzles of different shapes. (ii) Palette knife to smoothen icing and a sharp knife to slice the cake. (iii) Brushes, rolling pin and flower or biscuit cutters. (iv) Cake stand or turntable, cake pillars and cooling rack. (v) Cake combs and cake decorations such as ribbons, laces and flowers.

questions.q: How do you apply marzipan over a cake?
questions.answer: (i) Place the cake upside down on a prepared cake base and roll lightly to flatten the surface. (ii) Brush the top with apricot jam and dust with icing sugar. (iii) Roll out marzipan to 5 mm, invert the cake onto it and trim the excess. (iv) Brush the sides with apricot jam and fit pieces of rolled marzipan around the side. (v) Smooth the joins with a palette knife and leave in a warm, dry place before royal icing.

questions.q: Describe the basic process of icing a cake in four steps.
questions.answer: (i) Preparing a cake base: place the cake upside down on a foil covered cardboard base. (ii) Giving filling: cut the cake horizontally into two layers and fill. (iii) Applying icing evenly on top and sides with a palette knife and combing the sides. (iv) Piping and decoration with a piping bag and nozzles.

questions.q: State five precautions to be taken while preparing royal icing.
questions.answer: (i) Beat the egg whites and icing sugar with a fork, not an egg beater. (ii) Never use a plastic bowl. (iii) Keep the bowl and fork completely grease free. (iv) Use liquid colours instead of powder. (v) Use it fresh as its keeping quality is low; if stored, keep it in an airtight container in a dry place.
